head: codex/recovery-admission-20261012
title: fix: share recovery API budgets and repair original terminal debt
body:
## Scope

Reduce GitHub API amplification in the autonomous recovery admission path, make its quota budget visible across runners, and add a separate repair transition for an original reservation that is still RESERVED without its terminal.

## Changes

- Keep admission limited to the three actual authorization workflows. Each admission reads the exact triggering run by ID and attempt, then the exact attempt's jobs; skipped or irrelevant observers stop before approval/finalizer jobs. A rerun can resume the same admission while the original upstream run ID, attempt, repository, branch, and SHA remain pinned.
- Share the registered admission callers' GitHub Actions REST budget in the existing protected DynamoDB table. All three workflows bind one stable owner key to the repository ID, require the shared store, and assume their existing OIDC-scoped role. IAM permits only GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem on the exact budget partition. The limiter uses atomic compare-and-swap, fences concurrent readers, deduplicates a repeated operation ID, and fails closed on ambiguous writes.
- Keep GET-only reads bounded by a per-run invocation budget, response cap, timeout, concurrency and retry limits. Preserve Retry-After and primary reset evidence, defer 403/429 rate limits, save a nonauthorizing resume checkpoint, and retain generic permission-denied evidence without treating it as a producer failure or approval.
- Extend the repository mutation-boundary validator with an exact read-only admission exception, pinned OIDC role and repository-wide shared-budget checks, exact run/attempt/SHA binding, and mutation regressions; fix the per-role identity readback in all three admission workflows.
- Add a distinct, signed-quorum RESERVED-to-CONSUMED transition for the exact original reservation when terminal-null failure evidence exists. It writes only an immutable `ORIGINAL_TERMINAL_DEBT_ONLY` repair record and receipt. It cannot populate the normal original terminal, assert platform closure, or grant authority. Normal success and existing CONSUMED failure paths remain separately validated.
- Route the new repair actions through the real Lambda capsule and deployment boundary checks.

## Validation

Local validation passed: 41 Python ledger tests and 10 Python workflow-boundary tests; 7 targeted Node test files covering admission retries, rate waits, shared-budget CAS/DynamoDB identity checks, original terminal repair and immutable acknowledgement; 61 recovery-admission mutation regressions; AWS template and staging-deployment boundary validators; YAML parsing; syntax checks. These prove source behavior, not a deployed or natural operation.

## Remaining evidence and limits

The source and protected role policies are not merged or deployed. The shared quota is wired only for the three autonomous admission jobs; other workflows and direct GitHub API calls remain outside this registered coverage. No live protected run has yet shown the shared DynamoDB budget across runners or the original reservation from its original schedule through an immutable repair receipt. The actual original reservation remains unresolved until those natural-run and immutable-terminal checks pass. The repair receipt records debt-only reconciliation, never normal landing closure. Production, Public, G5, provider activation, Ready, approval, dispatch, merge and deployment remain outside this Draft's authority.

## Operating effects

- autonomous_effect: admit only eligible recovery work and resume a deferred admission under the same upstream identity.
- global_effect: coordinate a conservative read budget across three registered admission roles; broader API coverage remains unverified.
- irreplaceable_value_effect: preserve the exact original run, artifact, source and RESERVED row identity while recording an explicit debt-only repair transition.
- transparency_effect: retain rate-limit cause, retry time, API error evidence and the difference between debt reconciliation and normal closure.
